helpPageTitle: What to do after a scam – CyberGuard
helpTitle: A scammer may have my data – what now?
helpIntro: Stay calm. This can happen to anyone. Take the steps below right away – the sooner, the better.
helpBankTitle: Card, payment code or online banking details
helpBank1: Call your bank. The number is on the back of your payment card or in your banking app. Never call numbers from text messages or e-mails.
helpBank2: Ask them to block your card and your online banking access.
helpBank3: Check with the bank whether there are transfers or payments you did not make.
helpPasswordTitle: Password for e-mail, a shop or another site
helpPassword1: Change the password on the service's real website – ideally from another, trusted device.
helpPasswordSessions: Sign out of all devices – in your account settings (usually "Security" → "Sign out of all devices"). If a scammer took over your logged-in session, a new password alone is not enough – this cuts them off.
helpPassword2: If the same password works anywhere else, change it there too.
helpPassword3: Turn on two-step login (text message or app code) if the service offers it.
helpIdTitle: ID number, identity card details or a photo of a document
helpId1: In Poland: block your PESEL number in the mObywatel app or on gov.pl (search for: zastrzeż PESEL). It's free.
helpId2: Report the identity document as compromised at any bank branch (Dokumenty Zastrzeżone system) or at your local office.
helpRemoteTitle: Someone talked you into installing a program (e.g. AnyDesk, TeamViewer)
helpRemote1: Disconnect the computer from the internet and ask a trusted person to help remove the program. The scammer may be able to see and control your screen through it.
helpReport1: Report the page to CERT Polska:
helpReport2: In Poland, forward a suspicious text message free of charge to 8080.
helpReport3: If money is gone, also report it to the police (emergency number 112).
helpTalkTitle: Talk to someone close to you
helpTalk1: Scammers frighten and rush people so there is no time to think. There is nothing to be ashamed of – talking to someone you trust helps you go through these steps calmly.
helpCleanText: Removes history, cookies, cache and form data from the last hour.
helpCleanNote: Note: you will be logged out of some sites. This does NOT undo data that already reached the scammer and does not sign them out of your accounts – the steps above matter most.
helpCleanDone: Done. Data from the last hour has been removed.
helpCleanDenied: Data can't be cleared without the browser's permission.
helpCleanFailed: Could not clear the data. You can do it in the browser settings (Ctrl+Shift+Delete).
welcomeLead: There is nothing to set up. The extension works on its own:
welcome1: It stops known scam pages (CERT Polska and OpenPhish lists).
welcome2: It warns you when your bank, e-mail or government password is typed on a foreign site.
welcome3: It warns about pages pretending to be well-known companies.
welcomeNothingToDo: The shield icon next to the address bar tells you whether a page is known. You can close this tab now.
optFeedToggle: Download new CERT Polska warnings (every 12 hours)
optFeedPrivacy: The extension only downloads a public list. It never sends information about the pages you visit or about you.
optFeedError: The last attempt failed – we'll try again later.
optFeedBuilt: Protecting you from $1 dangerous pages (list from $2).
optFeedTotal: In total we protect you from $1 dangerous pages: $2 from the list built into the extension (from $3) and $4 new ones added by CERT Polska since then.
optFeedRemoved: $1 pages that CERT Polska withdrew from its list are no longer blocked.
optPasswordsText: CyberGuard does not store passwords. It keeps only a "fingerprint" that can't be turned back into the password, so it knows where each password is used.
optPasswordsEmpty: Nothing remembered yet. The list appears after your first login.
optForgetAllConfirm: Are you sure? Password protection will start learning from scratch.
optTrustedText: Sites where you clicked "I trust this site" or "Got it, don't show again". The warning about your bank or e-mail password always works, here too.
optAllowedTitle: Pages unblocked until the browser closes
optAllowedText: These pages are on the dangerous list but were unblocked. They will be blocked again when you close the browser.
optAbout1: CyberGuard checks everything on your computer. Passwords are never sent or stored anywhere.
optAbout2: Dangerous page lists: CERT Polska (hole.cert.pl) and OpenPhish.
